title: Versions of Windows
text:
EARLIER VERSIONS OF WINDOWS.
 WINDOWS 3.1
 Windows 3.1 is not an OS. In order to install and run Windows 3.1, it requires one to have DOS
 already installed on the computer.
 Windows 3.1 simply replaces the DOS interface, & changes the way in which the user
 communicates with the computer, gives commands, and works with the application programs.
 Since Windows 3.1 is not an OS, it does not perform the function of resource management. The
 Processor, Input/Output device & Disk management is handled by DOS. However, Memory
 management & Disk-caching are performed by Windows to improve the performance of
 Windows applications and to ensure efficient multi-tasking.
 Windows for Workgroups (WINDOWS 3.11).
 Windows 3.11 adds Networking capabilities & additional features to Windows 3.1.
 With Windows 3.11, you can connect to several PCs into a Peer-to-Peer network & be able to
 share resources (Files, Printers, Modems, etc), connect to other networks, and also send &
 receive E-mail and Faxes.
 Windows 3.11 has network programs such as, NetWatcher & Winmeter that enables one to
 monitor the performance of the system & also how other people are using the shared resources.
 Chat program allows one to communicate with other workgroup members by sending &
 receiving messages through typing.
 CURRENT VERSIONS OF WINDOWS.
 WINDOWS ‘95.
 Windows 95 is currently the defacto (actual / effective) OS for IBM compatible PCs. It came as
 an enhancement of Windows 3.11.
 It is a true 32-bit OS that manages the entire computer system, including its Screen, Keyboard,
 Disk drives, Memory & the Processor (i.e. it does not run on top of DOS).
 Windows 95 offers high performance & improvements to many familiar features in the earlier
 versions of Windows.
 (i). It is compatible with the previous DOS & Windows applications enabling those
 applications to run side by side with the newer 32-bit Windows 95 applications.
 (ii). New User Interface.
 - Has a Start button that provides easy access to programs, most recently used
 documents, and important system utilities such as Control Panel & Printers.
 - Easier to switch between programs using the Taskbar.
 - The look of the maximize & minimize buttons has been changed and a Close button has
 been added.
 (iii). Ability to handle Long File Names.
 Win ‘95 supports long file names; up to 32 characters, thus allowing the user to give files
 more meaningful names. This also makes the files easier to find and organize.
 (iv). Built-in Networking Support.
 Win ‘95 supports a wider choice of networks & has its own suite of transmission protocols.
 It has facilities for sharing files & devices, which are completely integrated in the
 Windows 95 user interface.
 (v). Integrated Mail and Fax support.
 Win ’95 includes Microsoft fax. It also includes Microsoft Exchange, which can be used to
 view & work with all types of electronic communications, including E-mail.
 (vi). Support for Mobile Computing.
 Win ‘95 supports Mobile computing with a file synchronization tool & a utility for
 transferring files over a direct cable link or dial-up networking.
 (vii). Win ‘95 allows true Multi-tasking, i.e. one can have several processes running in the
 background while he/she works.
 (viii). Improved Game & Multimedia Support.
 Win ‘95 has inbuilt sound, video & CD capabilities, and can fully support MS-DOS based
 games. It also has improved performance for playing video & sound files.
 (ix). Plug-and-Play Hardware compatibility.
 Win ’95 supports Plug-and-Play devices, which makes it easier to install new devices onto
 the system.
 WINDOWS ‘98.
 Win ‘98 is an enhancement of Win ‘95. It is similar to Windows 95 & all applications written
 for Win ‘95 are able to run without any modification under Windows 98. However, Windows 98
 doesn’t ‘crash’ as often as Win ‘95.
 Win ‘98 is able to support the latest graphics, sound & multimedia technologies. It enables easy
 addition & removal of peripheral devices with support for the Universal Serial Bus (USB). It
 also supports Web TV.
 Win ‘98 has a better interface to the Internet. The Active Desktop lets you place the Channel Bar
 & Internet components such as regularly updated news headlines right on the Windows desktop.
 Windows 98 even lets you set a Web Site as the desktop’s background paper.
 NEW FEATURES IN WINDOWS ‘98.
 1. Improved Web features.
 Windows 98 combines the power of the computer with the interactive content of the Internet
 thus improving the Web features:
  AutoComplete feature, which automatically completes previously visited Web addresses
 as you type them.
  Has an improved listing of favorite Web sites.
  Has improved tracking of Web sites visited.
  Supports all major Internet standards, including ActiveX, Java, etc.
  Improved performance with Dynamic HTML, which makes Web pages more interesting.
 New Internet support.
 The Internet Connection wizard helps you sign up for Internet service through an Internet
 Service Provider (ISP) & automatically handles the software configuration steps necessary for
 gaining access to the Internet.
 Active Desktop for displaying Web pages on the Desktop.
 Active Desktop makes it possible for you to customize your desktop, launch programs, switch
 between files & keep up with the latest World news by integrating the Web and your desktop.
 With Active Desktop, you can update your Web elements at any time.
 To make a Web-page picture your desktop wallpaper.
 1. Right-click the desktop, then click Properties.
 2. Open the Background tab, then click Browse.
 3. Click the HTML document you want, then choose Apply.
 The wallpaper appears on your desktop as tiled, stretched, or centered, depending on the
 current setting in the Display box.
 Tip. You can also right-click any graphic on a Web page, then click Set as Wallpaper.
 Browse the Web from anywhere.
 The Go & Favorites menus, which help you reach your favorite Web sites are found everywhere
 in Windows 98. E.g., they can be found on the Start menu or the Internet Explorer icon on
 your Taskbar.
 You can use the Address bar in Windows Explorer or add an Address bar to the Taskbar, and
 type an Internet address without first opening the browser.
 Microsoft Outlook Express for E-mail.
 Win ‘98 includes Microsoft Outlook Express, which provides features for e-mail and
 newsgroup communications.
 To start Outlook Express, click Start, point to Programs, then click Outlook Express.
 NetMeeting & Microsoft Chat for Internet Chatting.
 Win ’98 includes NetMeeting that helps one to hold digital conversations with family, friends,
 and business associates around the world. It can also assist you to work with a group of people
 from within any Windows-based program by sending text messages, and transferring files.
 With the correct hardware installed on your computer, you can also have live, face-to-face
 meetings.
 Microsoft FrontPage Express for creating Web Pages.
 FrontPage Express is a Web-page editor that helps you to create simple web pages & also copy
 your web pages to a web server.
 To start FrontPage Express, click Start, point to Programs, point to Internet Explorer, then
 click FrontPage Express.
 Power management.
 Power Management helps to save power resources by putting the computer on Standby or
 Hibernation.
 Power Management works on computers with Advanced Power Management (APM), and on
 computers that use the Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI).
 Universal Serial Bus (USB).
 The Universal Serial Bus makes the computer easier to use with advanced plug-and-play
 capabilities. Using the USB connector, you can add devices to your computer easily without
 having to restart.
 Accessibility wizard
 The Accessibility wizard makes it easier for people with disabilities to operate a computer
 without installing special software.
 Accessibility options—such as StickyKeys, ShowSounds, and MouseKeys—are designed to help
 users with specific disabilities make full use of the computer.
 • To start the Accessibility wizard;
 Click Start, point to Programs, point to Accessories, point to Accessibility, then click
 Accessibility Wizard.
 Help
 Win ‘98 has an Help system that makes a computer easier to use. With Help, you can find
 answers to your questions quickly & easily. You can also get up-to-date technical support from
 the World Wide Web.
 To start Help, click Start, then click Help. To get help from the Web, click Web Help at the top
 of the Help page.
 2. Improved reliability
 Windows 98 improves computer reliability by introducing new wizards, utilities, and
 resources such as, Windows Update that help keep your system running smoothly.
 Windows Update is a Web-based (online extension) of Windows 98 that helps your
 computer work & run better.
 Windows Update provides a central location to find and download product enhancements
 such as system files, device drivers, new Windows 98 features and specific files customized
 for your computer.
 • To open Windows Update, click Start, then choose Windows Update.
 -Or-
 Click Start, point to Settings, then click Windows Update.
 To add or change a device driver for hardware.
 1. Open Control Panel, then double-click System to open the System Properties dialog
 box.
 2. Click the plus sign (+) next to the type of hardware, and then double-click the hardware.
 3. On the Driver tab, click Update Driver, then follow the instructions on the screen.
 Note. Some devices do not have a Driver tab. In this case, change the driver by double-
 clicking the icon in Control Panel that is specific to that type of hardware.
 Putting toolbars where you want them.
 You can add toolbars to your Windows taskbar, making it even easier to get to your programs,
 files, folders, and favorite Web pages.
 The following toolbars can be added.
 (i). Quick Launch toolbar - provides shortcuts to several often-used features, including the
 desktop, the Web browser, and Outlook Express.
 (ii). Address toolbar - enables one to type a Web page address (URL) without first opening the
 Internet Explorer browser.
 one can open them without first opening the browser.
 (iv). Desktop toolbar - contains all of the shortcuts on your desktop and organizes them into one
 convenient place.
 To add a toolbar to the taskbar.
  Right-click a blank area on the Taskbar, point to Toolbars, then click Address, Links,
 Desktop, or Quick Launch.
 The selected toolbar appears on the Taskbar.
 3. A faster Operating system.
 Win ‘98 includes a suite of programs that help your computer run faster than Windows 95
 without adding new hardware.
 E.g., System tools like,
 - Maintenance wizard, which schedules Windows’ housekeeping programs such as
 Scandisk, Disk Cleanup, & Disk Defragmenter to run on regular basis.
 - Drive Converter (FAT32).
 4. More entertaining and fun.
 Win ‘98 makes your computer more entertaining by introducing new features such as
 enhanced television, video playback, and support for new hardware.
 (a). New hardware and graphics
 Windows 98 supports a variety of new hardware devices, such as USB & IEEE 1394
 devices, DVDs, force-feedback Joysticks, digital audio Speakers, recording devices and
 improved plug-and-play capabilities that make installing new hardware easier.
 (b). DirectX
 Win ‘98 includes DirectX, a utility that provides better playback of different types of
 Multimedia & manages 3-D graphics on your computer.
 (c). Desktop themes
 Win ‘98 includes 4 Microsoft themes—Underwater, Jungle, Baseball, & Space and the
 entire Microsoft Plus! for Windows 95 themes package.
 WINDOWS Me (Millennium Edition).
 Windows Me creates a mainstream OS that incorporates the best business features of Win ‘98 &
 builds on the strengths of Windows NT.
 The in-built features of Windows 98 include: - a simplified user interface, improved Plug-and-
 Play, Power management, & support for a broad range of hardware devices.
 Windows Me also builds on the strengths of Windows NT Workstation. This makes Windows
 Me secure, reliable, perform better, and manageable.
 OS/2.
 OS/2 is IBM’s GUI Operating System for Intel 8086 microprocessors. It is a 32-bit Single-user,
 Multi-tasking OS.
 OS/2 cannot support terminals since it is Single-user.
 OS/2 is more robust & faster than Windows 3.1 & Windows 3.11. When Multi-tasking under
 OS/2, the computer does not hang-up when one of the applications fails. However, the
 applications running on it are few and therefore, applications portability is a problem.
 NETWORK OPERATING SYSTEMS.
 A Computer Network is formed whenever more than one computer is connected together.
 A computer network usually has one computer reserved as the Server or “Mother” of all the
 other computers on the network. The network Operating system usually resides in the Server.
 Network Operating systems consist of several pieces of software that run in various devices
 connected to a computer network.
 A good network OS is required to provide the following services: -
 √ Client-Server capabilities.
 √ File sharing services.
 √ File/Directory Naming service, i.e., should provide efficient directory naming in the network.
 √ Print sharing services, e.g., print spooling and queue management.
 √ Mail services.
 √ Network management services, such as, setting up of users, adding resources & managing
 network failures.
 Advantages of Networking computers.
 (i). Sharing of file servers – files are stored in a centralized file server, making it possible to
 control who has access to which files & the nature of the access.
 (ii). Sharing of Printers. It enables several users to print using one Printer. Jobs can be stored
 in the print server until the printer is ready to accept the information. This reduces the
 user’s time wasted waiting for the printer.
 (iii). Sharing of powerful computers. It is possible to harness the computational power of a more
 powerful computer remotely.
 (iv). Sharing of communication ports. It provides access to shared communications ports such
 as, Modems.
 (v). Centralized backup. It solves the problem of maintaining regular backup of many
 computers by backing up only the file server.
 (vi). Electronic mail (e-mail). Networks enhance communication between people by use of fast
 electronic mails.
 Examples Network operating systems.
 WINDOWS NT.
 Windows NT (New Technology) is a true 32-bit OS, designed to run on Intel-based 32-bit
 microprocessors.
 There are 2 versions of Windows NT: -
  Windows NT Advanced Server.
  Windows NT Workstation. Windows NT Workstation is similar to Windows 95/98.
 Windows NT is technically superior to Windows 95/98. For instance, it is more secure and
 keeps buggy programs from crashing the whole PC.
 Windows NT is written to operate on both DOS & UNIX platforms, allowing applications to
 execute on different types of computers.
 With Windows NT, Networking is an integral part of the OS. Network management functions
 are generally simplified & easier to perform.
 Drawbacks of Windows NT.
 (i). It has limited hardware & software compatibility.
 (ii). Requires its own drivers for devices, such as Video cards, Printers, etc. This is because, the
 existing DOS, Windows 3.1, & Windows 95 drivers won’t be able to work.
 NOVELL NETWARE.
 It a Local Area Network (LAN) OS designed for IBM standard computers running MS-DOS,
 Windows, OS/2 or Macintosh computers.
 Novell Netware provides a means for connecting several computers together into computer
 network.
 It also gives all the computers on the network, the ability to access files, programs, printers, e-
 mail & other services (collectively called network Resources) that are attached to the network.
 In addition, Novell Netware has many features for security, backup, and network administration.
 The later versions of Netware offer connectivity options for a wide range of Mainframe and
 Minicomputers & support Wide Area Networking (WAN). This makes it possible to have large
 corporate networks spanning the globe.
 UNIX.
 UNIX was developed by the Bell Laboratories in U.S.A.
 UNIX belongs to the MATS (Multi Access Time-sharing Systems) family of Operating systems.
 Features.
 UNIX is a full Multi-tasking OS. Multi-tasking means that, the system can perform several
 tasks (called Processes) at the same time. This enables the user to give the system one or more
 tasks to perform “in the background” while he/she gets on with something else without having to
 wait for the task to finish.
 It is a Multi-user Time-sharing OS written mostly in C, making it easily portable between
 machines with different hardware facilities. Multi-user means that, more than one user can use
 the system at the same time.
 Has a sophisticated and powerful command interpreter called SHELL.
 UNIX is now widely used, as it has become the OS that represents the link between the majority
 of Mainframes, Minis, Workstations, PCs, Supercomputers and Networks.
 LINUX.
 Linux is a UNIX-type Operating system.
 It includes true Multitasking, Virtual memory, shared libraries, proper memory management and
 other features consistent with UNIX-type systems.
